reason: Verdict 'stays closed, nothing to build' is confirmed, but one supporting argument is wrong. Confirmed: x138/K2 (#37, #38) carry no DivNet veto; exp56/exp58 use the DivNet conv block only inside the DaughterNet insertion. The break-even arithmetic holds: FP:TP break-even = 1/J = 7.7 at lab J 0.129 (exp60 control pooled 16/25/83) and 2.8 at public J 0.36 (probe 26). The veto is DNVETO in disguise (closed R2S-3). The DivNet checkpoint is in-sample on train, so there is no honest lab bed, and the exp60 dumps lack DivNet p. It cannot meet R8 (27 Sep 12:00 + honest gate + new OK). It costs about +65 min of kernel time (exp39 ~100 vs ~35 min). The veto also rode along in exp51 (0.950 < x138+insertion 0.954), which is confounded but gives no sign that it helps. WRONG: 'the tie at ~68% dose means ~2.8:1 on public'. In the exp60 lab only 41 of 676 emitted forks (~6%) are evaluable, so most vetoes hit unannotated free forks. The division term has weight 0.1 and a handful of evaluable changes is buried under display rounding and noise, so a tie is compatible with any FP:TP ratio. The tie bounds the effect to under about 0.0015; it does not measure the ratio.
fix: Curator note on I-058: 'Not in x138/K2. Stays closed on x138: DNVETO-family (closed), no honest bed (the public DivNet is in-sample, and exp60 dumps have no DivNet p), R8 cutoff. The probe-20 tie bounds the effect below ~0.0015 but does not measure the FP:TP ratio, because about 94% of forks are unevaluable. The veto also rode in exp51 (0.950) with no visible gain.' Remove the 'public-read ratio ~2.8' claim. Nothing to build or submit.
realistic_gain: 0 (info only). A veto on x138 is expected to move the score by less than 0.001 on public and private, and the sign is unknown on low-J private embryos. It costs about +1 h of kernel time and has no pre-deadline path.
